summary: the cases of tests/run exfat under etude, against an exFAT driver that never sets VolumeDirty, one that leaves a removed file's clusters allocated, and one that records a large file's valid length one byte short

argv: sh tests/proofs/guest.sh make rach2 && sh tests/proofs/guest.sh copy ${WORK} rach2/kernel

faults.name: never-dirty
faults.summary: the boot sector's VolumeFlags written without VolumeDirty whatever the caller asks, so that neither a machine ended in the middle of a write nor a failed write leaves the volume marked dirty

faults.name: chain-kept
faults.summary: a removed file's cluster chain is never freed, so that the host's walk finds clusters allocated and reached by nothing

faults.name: valid-short
faults.summary: a file of 64 KiB or more is written to its directory entry with a ValidDataLength one byte short, so that its last byte reads as zero on the host and after a reboot
